claims.text: Pre-oxidizing a MoNbTaTiW-based refractory high-entropy alloy at 1000°C for 10 hours in a low-oxygen atmosphere will form a thin, uniform, adherent protective oxide scale.
The pre-formed oxide scale will remain protective during a subsequent 100-hour exposure at 1100°C in air.
The tailored oxide scale will be self-healing.
Protective Al2O3 or SiO2 enrichment is preferable in the pre-formed scale.
A stable, compact surface layer can reduce subsequent high-temperature oxidation.
The pre-formed oxide layer limits oxygen diffusion into the alloy.
Pre-oxidation suppresses the formation of rapidly growing, non-protective oxides.
Pre-oxidation suppresses oxide-scale spallation during service exposure.
The pre-oxidized alloy will have significantly lower mass gain than the untreated alloy after exposure at 1100°C in air.
The pre-oxidized alloy will retain better oxide-scale integrity than the untreated alloy.
Improved oxide-scale integrity will help maintain the alloy's structural stability during extended exposure.
Untreated refractory high-entropy alloys typically form rapidly growing, non-protective oxide scales with high mass gain.
Untreated refractory high-entropy-alloy oxide scales typically experience spallation.
The external oxide layer strongly influences oxidation mass-gain behavior in refractory high-entropy alloys.
Formation of a protective oxide layer can be associated with parabolic oxidation kinetics at 1100°C.
The proposed improvement should apply around 1100°C in air or another oxygen-rich atmosphere for approximately 100 hours.
The magnitude of the oxidation-resistance improvement depends on alloy composition and pre-oxidation conditions.

contradictions.description: The tested alloy is specified as MoNbTaTiW-based, while the desired and measured protective oxides are Al2O3 or SiO2. Neither Al nor Si is included in that stated alloy or introduced by the pre-oxidation intervention, so formation of those oxides is compositionally inconsistent with the proposed system.
